catalog_quote: [Hagemeijer 2013, APiCS survey 35, §4 Phonology] Ferraz (1979) argues that Santome is a stress language, but this claim has been rejected by Maurer, who argues that Santome, as well as Principense, and Angolar, are tone languages (Maurer 1995, 2008, 2009). [Hagemeijer 2013, APiCS datapoint 35-120 Tone] Ferraz (1979) claims that Santome lacks phonologically signficant tone, although it is used as a stylistic or emphatic device. Maurer (2008), however, argues that Santome has a simple tone system with a two-way contrast. ... Simple tone system, for lexical and grammatical distinctions ... bóbó vs. bóbò, kúlù vs. kúlú ... idiot vs. mulatto, unripe vs. dark ... Confidence: Very certain [Bandeira 2017: 258-259] Para Ferraz (1979: 25), o santome não apresenta tom fonologicamente significante. ... audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation is present verbatim at the stated locators in the held APiCS survey 35 (§4), APiCS datapoint 35-120, and Bandeira 2017 pp. 258-259 and 312-313. (2) The classification 'conflict' (Ferraz 1979 / Schang 2000 stress vs Maurer 1995/2008 two-tone) rests on a 2013 specialist survey/database entry (Hagemeijer, who codes tone 'Very certain' in the datapoint while reporting the dispute neutrally in the survey) and a 2017 comparative-historical dissertation that paraphrases the primaries with page cites and itself rejects the tonal analysis. The primaries on both sides (Ferraz 1979 grammar p. 25; Maurer 2008 pp. 253-261; Schang 2000 pp. 87-88) are not held and not openly available (T&F and Benjamins paywalls; HAL intranet-only; Lisbon repository unreachable). OpenAlex/S2
